FFN slot = FastMultiHeadLut(input_dim=384, n_heads=4, n_outputs=384, nap=8/256 cells, tph=128); routing anchors index the full 384-d input; tables emit the full 384-d output directly (heads summed). _fe_note:
FUNCTION-EMITTING CELLS, gaussian basis, K=24. Fork of exp_n_0136 (raw FastMultiHeadLut FFN, 1.20567 at 330.7M params) with the routing IDENTICAL -- input_dim 384, n_heads 4, nap 8 (256 cells), tph 128, same anchors, same gather -- and only the cell EMISSION changed. A cell stores basis-function parameters over the output-index axis instead of 384 independent values; its contribution is those functions evaluated at every index.

GAUSSIAN: W[c,i] = sum_k amp[c,k] * exp(-0.5*((i - mu[c,k])/sigma[c,k])^2), with mu, log_sigma and amp all learnable PER CELL -- 3K = 72 params per cell against 384 for a raw vector, 5.33x fewer. Means start on an even grid across the index axis with jitter, sigma at half the bump spacing.

This variant does NOT commute with the gather-sum: each cell has its own mu and sigma, so its curve shape cannot be pulled out of the sum over gathered cells. That is what makes it different in kind from a learned decompress, and it is also why it is the expensive one -- the table has to be materialised every forward.

fe_k is the knob to sweep. Measured at this shape: see the smoke numbers in the task report.
_run_note: SHORT DIAGNOSTIC RUN: 4,000 steps on the FULL 16,000-step LR schedule (warmup 0.1 x 16,000 = 1,600, cosine anchored to 16,000). The schedule is NOT recompressed to 4k -- the run is simply cut, exactly as exp_g_0037..0047 were, so this trajectory is comparable to those and to the first 4k of any 16k run of the same recipe. It therefore stops at 94% of peak LR having traversed ~6% of the cosine, and no full-anneal conclusion follows from it.
